title: Understand the Arch Linux boot process
summary: Arch Linux boots in stages: firmware (BIOS/UEFI) loads a boot loader, which loads the kernel and initramfs. The kernel then starts early userspace to mount the root filesystem, followed by late userspace where systemd starts services and login prompts.

steps.explain: The firmware (BIOS or UEFI) initializes hardware and launches a boot loader or the kernel directly.
The boot loader loads the Linux kernel and the initramfs image.
The kernel unpacks the initramfs into a temporary root filesystem (rootfs) and executes /init as PID 1.
Early userspace (initramfs) loads necessary modules and mounts the real root filesystem at /sysroot.
The system switches to the real root filesystem and starts the init process (systemd).
Late userspace starts services, getty (for login prompts), or a display manager (for graphical login).
